verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 22.94
verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.94

verses.pali: 10. Pupphavagga
verses.english: 10. Flowers

verses.pali: Pupphasutta
verses.english: Flowers

verses.pali: Sāvatthinidānaṁ.
verses.english: At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, lokena vivadāmi, lokova mayā vivadati.
verses.english: “Mendicants, I do not dispute with the world; it is the world that disputes with me.

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, dhammavādī kenaci lokasmiṁ vivadati.
verses.english: When your speech is in line with the teaching you do not dispute with anyone in the world.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, natthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ, ahampi taṁ ‘natthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: What the astute deem as not existing, I too say does not exist.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, atthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ, ahampi taṁ ‘atthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: What the astute deem as existing, I too say exists.

verses.pali: Kiñca, bhikkhave, natthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ, yamahaṁ ‘natthī’ti vadāmi?
verses.english: And what do the astute deem as not existing, which I too say does not exist?

verses.pali: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ natthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ; ahampi taṁ ‘natthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: Form that is permanent, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable.

verses.pali: Vedanā …
verses.english: Feeling …

verses.pali: saññā …
verses.english: Perception …

verses.pali: saṅkhārā …
verses.english: Choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ niccaṁ dhuvaṁ sassataṁ avipariṇāmadhammaṁ natthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ; ahampi taṁ ‘natthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: Consciousness that is permanent, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable.

verses.pali: Idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, natthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ; ahampi taṁ ‘natthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: This is what the astute deem as not existing, which I too say does not exist.

verses.pali: Kiñca, bhikkhave, atthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ, yamahaṁ ‘atthī’ti vadāmi?
verses.english: And what do the astute deem as existing, which I too say exists?

verses.pali: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ atthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ; ahampi taṁ ‘atthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: Form that is impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

verses.pali: Vedanā aniccā …pe…
verses.english: Feeling … Perception … Choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ atthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ; ahampi taṁ ‘atthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: Consciousness that is impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

verses.pali: Idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, atthisammataṁ loke paṇḍitānaṁ; ahampi taṁ ‘atthī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: This is what the astute deem as existing, which I too say exists.

verses.pali: Atthi, bhikkhave, loke lokadhammo, taṁ tathāgato abhisambujjhati abhisameti;
verses.english: There is a worldly phenomenon in the world that the Realized One understands and comprehends.

verses.pali: abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā taṁ ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti.
verses.english: Then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and reveals it.

verses.pali: Kiñca, bhikkhave, loke lokadhammo, taṁ tathāgato abhisambujjhati abhisameti, abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti?
verses.english: And what is that worldly phenomenon in the world?

verses.pali: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, loke lokadhammo taṁ tathāgato abhisambujjhati abhisameti.
verses.english: Form is a worldly phenomenon in the world that the Realized One understands and comprehends.

verses.pali: Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti.
verses.english: Then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and reveals it.

verses.pali: Yo, bhikkhave, tathāgatena evaṁ ācikkhiyamāne desiyamāne paññapiyamāne paṭṭhapiyamāne vivariyamāne vibhajiyamāne uttānīkariyamāne na jānāti na passati tamahaṁ, bhikkhave, bālaṁ puthujjanaṁ andhaṁ acakkhukaṁ ajānantaṁ apassantaṁ kinti karomi.
verses.english: This being so, what can I do about a foolish ordinary person, blind and sightless, who does not know or see?

verses.pali: Vedanā, bhikkhave, loke lokadhammo …pe…
verses.english: Feeling …

verses.pali: saññā, bhikkhave …
verses.english: Perception …

verses.pali: saṅkhārā, bhikkhave …
verses.english: Choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ, bhikkhave, loke lokadhammo taṁ tathāgato abhisambujjhati abhisameti.
verses.english: Consciousness is a worldly phenomenon in the world that the Realized One understands and comprehends.

verses.pali: Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti.
verses.english: Then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and reveals it.

verses.pali: Yo, bhikkhave, tathāgatena evaṁ ācikkhiyamāne desiyamāne paññapiyamāne paṭṭhapiyamāne vivariyamāne vibhajiyamāne uttānīkariyamāne na jānāti na passati tamahaṁ, bhikkhave, bālaṁ puthujjanaṁ andhaṁ acakkhukaṁ ajānantaṁ apassantaṁ kinti karomi.
verses.english: This being so, what can I do about a foolish ordinary person, blind and sightless, who does not know or see?

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uppalaṁ vā padumaṁ vā puṇḍarīkaṁ vā udake jātaṁ udake saṁvaḍḍhaṁ udakā accuggamma ṭhāti anupalittaṁ udakena;
verses.english: Suppose there was a blue water lily, or a pink or white lotus. Though it sprouted and grew in the water, it would rise up above the water and stand with no water clinging to it.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, tathāgato loke jāto loke saṁvaḍḍho lokaṁ abhibhuyya viharati anupalitto lokenā”ti.
verses.english: In the same way, though I was born and grew up in the world, I live having mastered the world, unsullied by the world.”

verses.pali: Dutiyaṁ.
